summary: Defines Session Description Protocol offer/answer procedures for setting up SCTP associations carried over DTLS, which is how WebRTC data channels run. It adds new SDP elements so two endpoints can agree on and negotiate this transport. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Two computers need to agree how to pass secret notes before they start. This document gives them the wording to say "let's send our messages this way, safely wrapped" so both sides set up the same thing.

questions: how is sctp over dtls negotiated in sdp
how are webrtc data channels set up in sdp
what is the sctp-port sdp attribute
what is the default max-message-size in sdp
subtitle: How two endpoints use SDP offer/answer to agree on an SCTP association carried over DTLS, the setup behind WebRTC data channels.

tldr.problem: RFC 8261 defines how SCTP runs on top of DTLS, but SDP had no way to describe that transport or to negotiate it with the offer/answer mechanism.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines two new SDP proto values, UDP/DTLS/SCTP and TCP/DTLS/SCTP, two new attributes (sctp-port and max-message-size), and the offer/answer rules for setting up, replacing and closing the SCTP, DTLS and TCP layers.
tldr.outcome: Endpoints can negotiate a single SCTP-over-DTLS association in SDP, for example for the webrtc-datachannel usage. It is a Proposed Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated.

today: RFC 8841 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2021. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
The Session Description Protocol (SDP) describes multimedia sessions. The Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) is a reliable transport that carries data between two endpoints in SCTP associations. RFC 8261 specifies how SCTP can run on top of the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol, called SCTP-over-DTLS.

This RFC fills the gap on the signaling side. It defines the proto values UDP/DTLS/SCTP and TCP/DTLS/SCTP and says how to use them with the SDP offer/answer mechanism of RFC 3264 to negotiate SCTP-over-DTLS associations.

One note matters early: TCP delivers everything ordered and reliably, so using TCP/DTLS/SCTP forces ordered, reliable delivery of SCTP packets and limits what SCTP options can do. The RFC therefore RECOMMENDS using TCP only where UDP traffic is blocked.
sections.eli5: Two programs want to send each other messages through a protected tunnel. This document teaches them how to agree on the tunnel using their opening message.

sections.title: The SDP Media Description
sections.content:
An SDP media line has the form m=<media> <port> <proto> <fmt>. The two new proto values describe the transport only, like the plain UDP and TCP values. UDP/DTLS/SCTP means an SCTP association on a DTLS association on UDP. TCP/DTLS/SCTP means the same on top of TCP.

An m= line with either value always describes a single SCTP association and MUST have exactly one fmt value. That value names the application usage of the whole association, is limited to the syntax of an RFC 4566 token, and MUST be registered with IANA. For WebRTC data channels it is webrtc-datachannel. The media field is application, and the port is the UDP or TCP port.

Describing individual SCTP streams inside an association is out of scope. RFC 8864 covers negotiating individual streams for WebRTC data channels.
sections.eli5: The opening message has a line that says what kind of tunnel you want and what you will use it for. There is exactly one purpose per line, like writing one subject on each envelope.

sections.title: The sctp-port and max-message-size Attributes
sections.content:
The new media-level attribute sctp-port carries the SCTP port, while the port on the m= line is the UDP or TCP port. It has no default: if it is missing, the m= line MUST be considered invalid. The range is 0 to 65535 and leading zeroes MUST NOT be used.

The attribute max-message-size gives, in bytes, the largest SCTP user message an endpoint is willing to receive. Each direction can differ. An endpoint MUST NOT send a message larger than the peer's stated maximum. A value of zero means messages of any size are handled, subject to memory capacity. If the attribute is absent, the default is 64K.

Both attributes have mux category CAUTION. Multiple SCTP associations over one DTLS association are outside this specification, so no mux rules are given.
sections.eli5: One setting says which numbered door to use. Another says the biggest parcel you will accept. If you do not say, the parcel limit is 64K, but the door number must always be given.

sections.title: Managing the Layers
sections.content:
The SCTP association, the DTLS association and the TCP connection are managed independently. Each can be set up and closed without affecting the others.

For SCTP, both endpoints MUST initiate the association, so both take the active role. Both MUST use the same SCTP port as client port and server port, which prevents two separate associations from forming. The SDP setup attribute therefore does not apply to the SCTP association, but it does apply to the DTLS association and the TCP connection. DTLS is managed per RFC 8842 and TCP per RFC 4145, where the holdconn value MUST NOT be used.

To replace an SCTP association, an endpoint signals a new, different SCTP port. To close one, it signals an sctp-port of zero. Neither action disturbs the underlying DTLS association. The SDP direction attributes (sendrecv and the like) MUST be ignored unless their semantics for the usage have been defined.
sections.eli5: The tunnel has layers, like a wrapped gift: box, paper and ribbon. You can swap the ribbon without redoing the box. Changing the port number swaps the inner layer only.

sections.title: Offer/Answer Procedures
sections.content:
Every endpoint MUST attach an SDP fingerprint (per RFC 8122) and a tls-id (per RFC 8842) to the m= line. Self-signed certificates can be used securely if the integrity of the SDP is assured.

The initial offer MUST include setup and sctp-port. For TCP/DTLS/SCTP it MUST also include connection with the value new. It MAY include max-message-size.

An answerer that accepts MUST echo the same proto value, include setup and sctp-port, and MAY include max-message-size, whose value is independent of the offer. If the offer used a new port, the answer MUST use a new port too. If the offer had port zero, or the answerer refuses the association, the answer MUST carry a zero SCTP port. If the answerer rejects the m= line it sets that line's port to zero.

After the answer, both sides follow the relevant RFC 4145 and RFC 8842 procedures to bring up or replace TCP and DTLS, then initiate the SCTP association. To change a session, the offerer uses a new SCTP port to replace, zero to close, or a zero m= port to tear down SCTP, DTLS and TCP together. The text defines no way to close DTLS while keeping SCTP.
sections.eli5: One side makes an offer with all its settings. The other side answers with the same kind of tunnel and its own settings. Then both start building at the same time.

sections.title: Example Exchange
sections.content: The RFC gives an offer and answer for UDP/DTLS/SCTP. The offerer uses UDP port 54111, SCTP port 5000, setup:actpass (it can take either DTLS role) and a max-message-size of 100000. The answerer uses UDP port 64300, SCTP port 6000 and setup:passive, so it takes the server DTLS role. Both use the webrtc-datachannel format.
sections.eli5: One side says it will use door 5000 and can play either role. The other says door 6000 and picks the role of the host.

sections.title: NAT, ICE and Multihoming
sections.content:
SCTP-over-DTLS relies on the NAT traversal of the underlying UDP or TCP. With UDP-based ICE candidates the UDP/DTLS/SCTP procedures apply, and with TCP-based ones the TCP/DTLS/SCTP procedures apply.

Implementations MUST treat all ICE candidate pairs for an SCTP association as part of the same DTLS association. There is only one SCTP handshake and one DTLS handshake, and switching pairs, even between UDP and TCP, does not disturb them. Implementations MUST be ready to receive data on any candidate. ICE-enabled endpoints SHOULD implement UDP/DTLS/SCTP, UDP candidates SHOULD be offered, and the proto value MUST match the transport of the default candidate.

Multihoming is not supported, because DTLS does not expose address management of the underlying transport to its upper layer.
sections.eli5: If the road changes, say you move from mobile data to WiFi, the conversation continues in the same tunnel. Only the road underneath changes.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
This specification adds no new security considerations beyond those of SDP, offer/answer, SCTP and SCTP-over-DTLS. It points to RFC 4566, RFC 3264, RFC 4145, RFC 8122, RFC 4960 and RFC 8261.

IANA registered the two proto values and the two attributes. It also created an association-usage registry with the First Come First Served policy of RFC 8126. The first entry is webrtc-datachannel, referencing RFC 8832 and this RFC.
sections.eli5: The tunnel is protected by the same locks as before, so nothing new needs guarding. A public list records what each tunnel type is for.
